summary: Suzanne Karpelès was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at INALCO, EPHE, and under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Finot. She held posts at the EFEO, National Library of Cambodia, and Buddhist Institute.

Suzanne Newcombe works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Amherst College, the LSE, and the University of Cambridge. Her career includes posts at Cambridge, the LSE, Inform, and Open University.

Suzanne Siauve was an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied at ENS de Sèvres, under Louis Renou and Jacques Bacot, and earned a Ph.D. from the University of Paris. She held posts at Lycée Jeanne-d'Arc, CNRS, and Institut de France.

Sven Hedin worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Stockholm, Uppsala, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Halle-Wittenberg, and under Ferdinand von Richthofen.

Sven S. Hartman specialized in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala University under Nyberg, Wikander, and Widengren, and later held academic posts at Uppsala, Åbo Akademi University, and Lund University.
Sven Sellmer works in Indology, linguistics, and computational fields. He has held academic posts at the University of Düsseldorf and Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań.
Sven Wittemann is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Kapila Abhayawansa.

Svetozar Petrović was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Zagreb and studied Indology at the University of Allahabad, later serving on the faculties of Zagreb, the University of Novi Sad, and the University of Belgrade.

Swami Japasiddhananda works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Sri Chamarajendra Sanskrit College, Karnataka State Open University, and Visva-Bharati University, later holding posts at Ramakrishna Math Vivekananda Veda Vidyalaya and RKMVERI.

Swami Lakshman Joo was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar. He studied under Maheshwar Nath Razdan, founded the Universal Shaiva Fellowship in 1991, and taught scholars including Silburn, Padoux, Bäumer, Singh, Sanderson, and Dyczkowski.

Swami Maheshanandagiri Maharaj works in philosophy and Indology. He served as Mahamandaleshvar Pontiff at Dakshinamurti Peetha and founded both the Mahesh Research Institute and Advaita Grantha Ratna Manjusha.
Swami Satyananda Puri was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at and held a post at the University of Calcutta, and he taught Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara.

Swami Shivananda was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who studied at Thanjavur Medical College. He founded the Divine Life Society and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy, and taught Mircea Eliade, Hsiang-Kuang Chou, and Swami Vishnudevananda.
Swami Siddheswarananda was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Madras and held a post in the Ramakrishna Order from around 1920 to 1957.
Swami Vimalananda was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Ripon College and became a disciple of Swami Vivekananda in 1897.
Swami Vishnudevananda worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied as a disciple under Swami Shivananda from around 1947 to 1957 and founded the International Sivananda Yoga Vedanta Centres.

Swami Vivekananda was a philosophy, religious studies, and Indology figure. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta under Ramakrishna, and taught numerous students including Margaret Elizabeth Noble.

Swayam Bagaria works in religious studies and Indology. He earned degrees from Grinnell College and Johns Hopkins University, later holding a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of Virginia and an assistant professorship at Harvard University.
Sweta Prajapati is an Indology scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. She held director posts at the university and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara.

Sybrandus Johannes Warren was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later served as director of Johan de Witt-gymnasium and Erasmiaans Gymnasium.
